# Content Calendar for Small Teams: A Simple System

Most small teams do not fail at content because of bad ideas. They fail because the content calendar lives in someone's head. This guide shows the system we use with clients who publish twice a week with two people.

## Start with three topic clusters

Pick three topics your buyers search for before they buy. Each cluster gets one pillar page and four to six supporting posts. We tested this with 14 client sites and the clusters with a pillar page got 38% more clicks after six months.

Write the clusters down with one keyword per post. If two posts share a keyword, merge them before you write anything.

## Choose a cadence you can keep

Two posts a week is plenty for most teams. A steady cadence beats bursts. When we tried three posts a week, quality dropped and edits took twice as long.

Put publishing on fixed days, such as Tuesday and Thursday. Your readers learn the rhythm and your writers know the deadline.

## Write briefs one week ahead

A brief takes 20 minutes and saves hours. It names the reader, the search intent, the keyword, three questions the post must answer and the internal links to add.

Use the [brief template](/templates/content-brief/) and link every new post to its pillar page.

## Review the calendar every month

Once a month, look at what shipped and what slipped. Move topics, retire weak ideas and check which older posts need a refresh. Google's [Search Console help](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553) explains the performance report we use for this.

## What to do next

Copy the template, fill in your three clusters and schedule the next eight weeks. Then protect the publishing days like client meetings.
